correctness.rationale: For the explicit rank-one partial isometry K, the Moore--Penrose inverse, the projection P, both unitary factorizations, the common synthesis matrix, the Parseval identity, and the two distinct proposed Grassmannian images are all exact. The same ordered frame is used for both factorizations, so the failure is genuinely failure of well-definedness. The canonical identity R(T_F^*)=U_F^*R(K^*) follows directly from T_F=KPU_F and PK^*=K^*.

value.rationale: The correspondence is a headline structural result of the paper, and the defect occurs in the smallest nontrivial dimension with a rank-one partial isometry and two nonzero frame vectors. The same frame is sent to two orthogonal Grassmannian points, so the construction fails before questions of injectivity or surjectivity. Identifying the canonical analysis-range invariant R(T_F^*) also isolates exactly which range is determined by the frame data.
